minutes.headline: Sewer Commission took no vote on the Pond View 40B sewer route but told the developer it prefers Beale Street to Leominster.
minutes.summary: The commission heard Kevin O'Brien of Pond View Estates ask which path the sewer line should take; members voiced a preference for Beale Street to Leominster, subject to peer review, and said legal questions are for the attorneys and the town. They also heard staff reports on 361 Mass Ave, the draft environmental policy, grease traps, and a billing waiver request, which members agreed to authorize.

public_comment.topic: Asked what the peer review plan is, whether the information is public, and urged the commission to hold its position against the project.

Matthew (Allison) said he was pleased no vote was taken, argued the 40B applicant should not design the town's sewer system and the matter is for the ZBA, and urged looking at low-pressure effluent systems like Westford's and serving unserved residences in the service area.

votes.motion: Authorize waiver/credit of a sewer bill for a homeowner with an unmetered garden irrigation, based on average usage (a motion was invited; agreement appears by consensus).

votes.outcome: passed (roll call: Mike aye, Dave aye, chair aye)

budget_items.topic: Sewer bill waiver for irrigation use
budget_items.what_was_said: A homeowner's billed amount was far above average because of garden watering with no irrigation meter; the business manager proposed reducing it to average usage and members agreed.
The chair noted the existing sewer district cost the town a large sum, questioning whether a new district would be needed.
Members asked about the status of the town's allocation of funds; the town replied no update and the commission may write again.
Unpaid invoices from the prior fiscal year are going onto tax bills.

budget_items.topic: Flow meter for 361 Mass Ave project
budget_items.what_was_said: Members suggested a flow meter at the connection to measure sewer flow given rainwater reuse.

decisions.decision: Members agreed by consensus to authorize the business manager to credit the homeowner's sewer bill to average usage.
O'Brien will design the force main toward Beale Street/Leominster and submit a plan for peer review.
Keep the end-of-December meeting date open pending the 40B hearing the next night.
Hold a policy workshop in January, with the date to be set once Barbara returns.
Business manager directed to restart the non-compliance process for the grease trap violator.
Bill to check whether the funding allocation has a year-end deadline.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission took no vote on the Pond View 40B sewer route, but members told the developer's representative they prefer a line toward Beale Street and Leominster.
The developer's representative will design the force main toward Beale Street and Leominster and submit the plan for peer review.
Members agreed by consensus, with no audible vote, to have the business manager credit a homeowner's sewer bill down to average usage after unmetered garden irrigation.
The business manager was directed to restart the non-compliance process for a grease trap violator.
The commission left its end-of-December meeting date open and planned a January policy workshop, with the date to be set.

why_it_matters: The route a 40B development's sewer line takes decides which streets and which part of the sewer service area carry the connection, and the commission's stated preference is not a binding decision.
A 40B project's sewer plan is reviewed by the commission, the Zoning Board of Appeals and the town's attorneys, so the commission's preference is one input into a decision made elsewhere.
Sewer bill credits and unpaid sewer invoices placed on tax bills affect what individual ratepayers and property owners owe.
watch_next: The 40B hearing held the night after this meeting, which determines whether the end-of-December commission meeting goes ahead.
